newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn to hit EMU goals without reserves move - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Bonn to hit EMU goals without reserves move - Waigel.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Saturday Germany would meet the convergence criteria for European monetary union (EMU) independently from plans to revalue the Bundesbank's gold and currency reserves.
Waigel also said that revaluation of the central bank's gold and foreign exchange reserves would not create any danger of increasing money supply or inflation.

"We are in a position, independent of the question of revaluing the gold reserves, to meet the Maastricht criteria," Waigel told reporters after a meeting with his counterparts from Austria and Switzerland.
Waigel added that his plan to revalue Bundesbank reserves in line with their market worth was "completely legitimate and accords with international practice".

Waigel has said that the revaluation would help cut the national debt and reduce the budget deficit, although the plan has raised suspicions among Germany's European partners that Bonn was resorting to creative accounting to qualify for EMU.

Bonn's efforts to qualify for EMU suffered a big setback last week when new tax revenue estimates revealed a new hole in state finances of nearly 20 billion marks this year. Waigel has vowed to meet the Maastricht treaty's budget deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product this year to qualify for the planned start of EMU in 1999.
